title: Variance and inverse relationship restored
diagnosis: The old translation misread the blue variance annotation as coefficient bias and dropped the inverse in the black prose.
correction: Restored variance and inverse relationship; no purple source-error note for the old reading.

title: Mediator annotation resolved
diagnosis: The lower graph margin reads that controlling W also has a negative effect; it is not an unreadable extra claim.
correction: Translated the visible annotation without the old unclear-phrase marker.

title: Unresolved implementation abbreviation retained
diagnosis: The old English rendered an uncertain handwritten abbreviation as JS, suggesting JavaScript without adequate scan evidence.
correction: Removed the unsupported JS expansion and retained an explicit uncertainty marker.

title: Zero selection bias identifies ATT, not automatically ATE
diagnosis: The blue arrow moves from ATT to ATE after only setting baseline selection bias to zero.
correction: Add treatment-effect mean independence or full randomization for ATT=ATE.

title: Sampling probability and confidence coverage
diagnosis: The scan uses P(data|H0), an informal confidence-probability description, and a general SE formula.
correction: Specify tail probability, repeated-sample coverage, and that s/sqrt(n) is the iid mean SE.

title: Graphical separation and dependence
diagnosis: The scan asserts dependence from an open path and groups mediator adjustment with collider selection.
correction: Use causal Markov d-separation for independence; open paths permit dependence and require faithfulness for converse; mediator adjustment changes total effect.

title: Direction of the residual regression
diagnosis: The black handwriting defines residual T by regressing covariates on treatment, opposite to FWL; the blue note supplies the intended direction.
correction: Regress T on X and residualize treatment.

title: Regression adjustment still needs identification
diagnosis: The all-confounders statement is too broad if read without functional-form and causal assumptions.
correction: Require exchangeability, positivity, consistency, and correct adjustment model; OVB equation also assumes residual orthogonality.

title: Normalize the subgroup regression weights
diagnosis: Variance-weighted subgroup statement is correct in the saturated group-intercept setup but its normalization is unstated.
correction: State P(G=g)Var(T|g) weights and common-slope setup.

title: Precision, bad controls, and participation
diagnosis: The scan loosely uses outcome variance for coefficient precision and inverse variance for SE, and its zero/positive decomposition silently excludes negative outcomes.
correction: Specify homoskedastic SE formula and Y nonnegative; retain author intuition as precision and overcontrol claims.

title: Exclusion is not conditional observed-outcome independence
diagnosis: The source asks whether Y independent Z given T is an IV requirement and already marks it inaccurate in red.
correction: Use potential-outcome exclusion and instrument exogeneity.

title: IV ratios and finite-sample claims
diagnosis: Calculus analogy and finite-sample 2SLS statements are written without their regimes.
correction: Keep covariance derivation for linear constant effect; derivative analogy and weak-IV consistency require conditions.

title: Non-strict monotonicity and the LATE label
diagnosis: Strict inequality for every unit excludes the never- and always-takers drawn in the source; the Wald ratio is labeled ATE.
correction: Use T1>=T0 almost surely with positive complier probability; label identified estimand LATE.

title: Matching bias and the estimand
diagnosis: The scan uses a single generic i in the root-n bias expression and says correction ensures convergence without conditions.
correction: State average conditional matching discrepancy, overlap, smoothness, and distinction consistency/root-n behavior.

title: Balancing is not equivalent to ignorability
diagnosis: The original double arrow equates a propensity balancing identity with potential-outcome independence.
correction: Balancing is not equivalent to ignorability. Conditional exchangeability given X implies exchangeability given e(X); overlap is separately required for identifying both treatment-arm means, not for that independence theorem.

title: Weighted dispersion is not the IPW estimator variance
diagnosis: The source labels a weighted outcome variance IPTW and gives an unexplained 20 percent threshold.
correction: Distinguish dispersion from sampling variance; no universal weight cutoff.

title: Doubly robust cancellation is conditional
diagnosis: The blue source writes E[mu1(X_i)]=Y_i and unconditioned residual cancellation.
correction: Replace pointwise cancellation by conditional expectation; explain both correctness routes.

title: Parallel trends is an identifying assumption
diagnosis: The source writes potential-outcome growth independent of D and a shorthand unit-level counterfactual equality.
correction: Use equality of untreated mean trends and no anticipation; explain FE conditions.

title: Aggregate panels and synthetic-control identification
diagnosis: The source motivates SC by asserting panel methods need disaggregated data, and convexity is presented as protection from overfitting.
correction: Clarify aggregate panels work; convexity limits extrapolation but does not establish causal validity.

title: Placebo tail probability and its denominator
diagnosis: The source says higher while its negative-effect inequality counts lower effects; quoted 0.0286 denominator is absent.
correction: Use lower-tail rank for negative effect, include observed assignment for exact randomization p, and require exchangeability.

title: Center the running variable before reading the intercept
diagnosis: The source writes an uncentered RDD interaction model then equates beta2 with cutoff jump.
correction: Uncentered jump beta2+beta3*c; centered model jump beta2.

title: RD locality, fuzzy compliance, and density tests
diagnosis: Local random experiment, attenuation, and McCrary spike descriptions need precise conditions.
correction: Continuity-based RD differs from literal randomization; fuzzy ratio needs local IV assumptions; density test concerns jump.

title: Nonsignificance does not imply a small effect
diagnosis: The scan directly infers a small effect from large p.
correction: Effect magnitude and uncertainty determine significance jointly.

title: Include perfect fit in the R-squared range
diagnosis: The original range excludes the value 1.
correction: For nonconstant outcomes R2<=1 inclusive; can be negative out of sample.

title: Causal conditional means and elasticity units
diagnosis: The source optimizes an observational conditional mean and calls a raw derivative elasticity.
correction: Use interventional response under ignorability; derivative is sensitivity unless scaled by t/y.

title: Evaluate the ranking on an identified effect
diagnosis: The notes mention observational fitting but do not explicitly state the randomized evaluation requirement; cumulative means and negative slopes are underspecified.
correction: Use independent identified evaluation, subset-specific means and appropriate sign convention.

title: Assignment independence uses treatment, not covariates
diagnosis: The original writes potential outcomes independent X as if sufficient for comparability.
correction: Replace with randomized treatment independence or conditional exchangeability.

title: CATE risk and individual-effect risk differ
diagnosis: The scan equates squared CATE error with squared individual-effect error.
correction: Add irreducible conditional treatment-effect variance.

title: What transformed outcomes are unbiased for
diagnosis: The source calls the transformed target unbiased for individual effects and downplays variance at large N.
correction: Under conditional ignorability it has conditional mean CATE; finite second moments/overlap still needed.

title: Continuous-treatment proof needs conditional moments
diagnosis: The proof uses sample means as if fixed population moments and assumes the global treatment variance works conditionally.
correction: State population conditional centering and linear conditional response; sample version asymptotic or cross-fit.

title: A squared individual residual is not treatment variance
diagnosis: The handwritten proposed extension uses M(T_i) although M predicts T from X and divides by a single squared residual.
correction: Use conditional residual variance; retain ratio only as weighted R-loss re-expression with caveats.

title: Meta-learner identification and X-learner weights
diagnosis: The source algorithms are correct but causal conditions and the status of e(x) as a weighting choice are unstated.
correction: Require exchangeability/overlap; propensity combination is useful not universally optimal.

title: Residual regression is not always the ATE
diagnosis: The source labels constant residual slope ATE and treats cross-fitting as sufficient to remove bias.
correction: Give heterogeneous slope weighted estimand and nuisance-rate requirements.

title: R-loss alone does not identify a local derivative
diagnosis: The handwritten final claim says DML finds a derivative at X for nonlinear treatment response; textbook contains the same overstatement.
correction: Its population target is a conditional projection slope; derivatives require additional modeling/localization.

title: Prediction residual has the subtraction reversed
diagnosis: The supplement literally instructs predicted T minus Tnew although training uses T minus predicted T.
correction: Use r_new=Tnew-mhat(X) and predict residual outcome, not price.

title: Keep the unfinished nonlinear idea as a proposal
diagnosis: The source labels its residual nonlinear construction unfinished and CATE with a question mark.
correction: Interpret conditional outcome curve under identification, without transferring orthogonality guarantees.

title: The written simulation does not produce the quoted conversion effect
diagnosis: The scan follows textbook prose G(20,2) and threshold zero, but textbook code scales income by 100 and uses threshold 0.1.
correction: Separate handwritten DGP from reproduced code; latent ATE 1.4 valid, conversion 0.39477 is sample difference from other DGP.

title: Low baseline conversion does not always mean a large effect
diagnosis: The final handwritten line repeats high baseline and says low conversion has high effect, conflicting with both-tail saturation explanation.
correction: Give probit threshold contrast and explain small effects at both extremes.

title: A power transform is a model proposal
diagnosis: The source proposes a negative price power to linearize a nonlinear response; exponent is not fully certain.
correction: Retain tentative transform and require empirical/structural verification and chain rule.

title: Collider and descendant labels restored
diagnosis: Magnification shows X->W2<-Y and W2->W1, not an unspecified W with two proxies.
correction: Restored the precise node labels and the descendant arrow in the translated graph.

title: Matrix products must follow the stated layout
diagnosis: The source explicitly puts observations in rows and features in columns, and describes beta as a row vector, but writes incompatible beta*X matrix products.
correction: Use X1*beta1^T+X2*beta2^T with the source row-vector convention, or explicitly adopt column coefficients and use X1*beta1+X2*beta2. Fitted values are the corresponding projection products.

title: The blue annotation says unrelated
diagnosis: Magnified scan reads X unrelated to outcome; the old translation incorrectly said related.
correction: Translated the original statement as unrelated; its mathematical assertion is reviewed separately.

title: An irrelevant covariate does not automatically bias OLS
diagnosis: The original blue margin asserts beta1 and beta3 become biased when X is unrelated to outcome.
correction: Under a correctly specified exogenous linear model irrelevant covariates need not create bias; distinguish variance and regularization.
